findings.message: references 8 action or reusable workflow ref(s) that are not pinned to a full commit SHA
findings.remediation: Pin third-party actions and reusable workflows to a full 40-character commit SHA.
findings.impact: Mutable action refs can change without a workflow diff if the upstream tag or branch is moved.
findings.attack_vector: A workflow uses @main, @master, a version tag, or another ref instead of a full commit SHA.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Review extremely long lines; they may contain hidden logic.
findings.impact: Extremely long lines hide obfuscated or minified code from human review.
findings.attack_vector: Lines > 500 chars — code is structured to evade visual inspection.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: modifies shell initialization files (2 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval for any shell profile modification.
findings.impact: Shell startup files can execute added commands in future terminal sessions.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a shell rc file; this low lead does not by itself prove a write occurs.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: passes request-controlled input directly to a dynamic code evaluation API
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and dispatch request values through a fixed allowlist of implementations.
findings.impact: Request-controlled dynamic evaluation can execute arbitrary code within the plugin process.
findings.attack_vector: A request body, query, parameter, header, argv, or input value reaches eval() or Function().
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: accesses system or user credential stores
findings.remediation: Avoid direct access to credential files; use authenticated API flows instead.
findings.impact: Direct access to system credential stores allows theft of SSH keys, AWS creds, and Docker tokens.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: reads sensitive system or credential files
findings.remediation: Never read system files, credential stores, or environment files from plugins.
findings.impact: Reading system credential files exposes SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and Docker tokens.
findings.attack_vector: File path matches /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials — secrets are read into memory.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: attempts path traversal with encoded or nested patterns
findings.remediation: Use path.resolve() and verify the result stays within the workspace root.
findings.impact: Path traversal with encoded patterns (%2e%2e%2f) or nested ../.. can escape any path-based sandbox.
findings.attack_vector: URL-encoded or nested traversal sequences — bypass naive path validation that only checks single ../.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: contains a command that can destructively alter the host system (2 occurrences in this file)
findings.basis: CWE destructive file or directory permissions
